"'''Together Again'''" is a song by American singer [[Janet Jackson]] from her sixth [[studio album]], ''[[The Velvet Rope]]'' (1997). It was written and produced by Jackson and [[Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis]], with additional writing by Jackson's then-husband [[René Elizondo Jr.]] It was released as the second [[Single (music)|single]] from the album in December 1997 by [[Virgin Records]]. Originally written as a [[ballad]], the track was rearranged as an uptempo [[Dance music|dance]] song. Jackson was inspired to write the song by her own private discovery of losing a friend to [[AIDS]], as well as by a piece of fan mail she received from a young boy in [[England]] who had lost his father.

"Together Again" was well received by [[Music journalism|music critics]], who praised the song's structure and Jackson's vocals. The single was a commercial success, topping the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] for two weeks, as well as reaching number one on the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Dance Club Songs|Dance Club Play]] chart. The single was additionally certified [[RIAA certification|platinum]] by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA). Worldwide, it peaked within the top five in many countries, such as Canada and the United Kingdom, and topped the charts in the Netherlands. The single sold six million copies worldwide.<ref>{{cite book|title= FYI > Together Again |publisher= [[Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS|UNAIDS Outlook Report]] |date= July 2010 |page= 30 |isbn= 9789291738595 |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=E1jwF1bK1tQC&q=%22together+again%22+%22six+million+copies+worldwide%22&pg=PA30}}</ref>

Two music videos were produced for "Together Again". The video for the original, directed by [[Seb Janiak]], shows Jackson and her dancers performing in a futuristic African paradise where people are seen living side by side with wild animals such as [[elephant]]s, [[giraffe]]s, and [[wildcat]]s. Another video released for the 'Deeper Remix', was directed by Elizondo Jr. and shows Jackson in an apartment. Jackson performed "Together Again" in a number of occasions to promote ''The Velvet Rope'', including at the [[American Music Awards of 1998|American Music Awards]] and also on all of her tours since its release. It is also included in two of her [[Greatest hits album|greatest hits collections]], ''[[Number Ones (Janet Jackson album)|Number Ones]]'' (2009) and ''[[Icon: Number Ones]]'' (2010).

Originally written as a [[Sentimental ballad|ballad]], the track was re-arranged as a [[dance music|dance]] and [[house music|house]] song. Jackson was reportedly inspired to write the song from her own personal experience, as well as a piece of fan-mail she received from a young boy in England who had lost his father.<ref name="Jacksons Number Ones">{{cite book|last=Halstead|first=Craig|author2=Chris Cadman |title=Jacksons Number Ones|publisher=Authors On Line|year=2003|pages=119, 120|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tynOwh1E_GAC|isbn=0-7552-0098-5}}</ref> According to [[Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis|Jimmy Jam]], "it had a deep meaning for her because it was about a friend she lost to AIDS, but as with all her songs, she tries to make them apply in a general sense to anybody. The idea was to make it a joyous song musically".<ref name="The Inside Story">{{cite book  | last = Bronson| first =  Fred | title = The Billboard Book of Number One Hits | publisher = Billboard Books | year = 2003 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=PgGqNrqfrsoC | isbn = 0-8230-7677-6 | page = 862}}</ref>

The arrangement of the song was constructed in 30 minutes by Jam, Terry Lewis, and Jackson while in the recording studio. sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
"Together Again" received positive reviews. [[BBC]] deemed it a "thumping great hit, an old-fashioned piece of professional dance music, played perfectly".<ref name=bbc>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/music/reviews/pnhf|title=Review of Janet Jackson - The Velvet Rope|access-date=June 17, 2014|publisher=[[BBC]]}}</ref> Larry Flick from ''Billboard'' magazine called it a "gorgeous disco ode to loved ones lost to AIDS-related illnesses". Jackson "has clearly been studying [[Donna Summer]] records, delivering a wonderfully nuanced performance that takes firm command of the track's vibrant house beat without sacrificing an ounce of emotion".<ref name=billboard>{{cite magazine|last=Flick|first=Larry|title=Revies & Previews|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7QkEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA76|date=October 8, 1997|access-date=June 24, 2014|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|issn=0006-2510|volume=43|issue=107|pages=76|location=New York}}</ref> Music critic Joey Guerra from ''[[The Daily Cougar]]'' stated, "Jackson pours her heart into "Together Again," which builds to an ecstatic house beat" which takes "a cue from the soaring melodies of '60s girl groups". He further commented that the song is "genuine happy-feeling. It sounds lame at first but pay attention to what she's singing; that vocal smile changes everything."<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archive.thedailycougar.com/vol63/29/Enter1/29100697/29100697.html|title=Janet Jackson swings both ways on The Velvet Rope|work=[[The Daily Cougar]]|access-date=June 17, 2014|publisher=Department of Student Publications}}</ref> A reviewer from ''[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]'' said, "[[Michael Jackson|Michael]]'s wee sis has never sounded so good. Janet has found herself and her sound."<ref>"Chart Slot". ''[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]''. December 12, 1997.</ref>

"She even makes a bid for [[gay icon]] status", wrote Neil McCormick in a review of ''The Velvet Rope'' for ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]'', "delivering a diva-ish performance reminiscent of [[Diana Ross]] on 'Together Again'."<ref>{{Cite journal|last=McCormick|first=Neil|title=The Arts: Give her enough rope ... Reviews Rock CDs|journal=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|page=11|date=October 18, 1997|issn=0307-1235}}</ref> [[J. D. It was Jackson's first single to reach number one in the U.S. since "[[Again (Janet Jackson song)|Again]]" in 1993.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/charts/1998-01-31/hot-100|title=The Hot 100: Jan 31, 1998|date=January 31, 1998|access-date=June 24, 2014|magazine=Billboard}}</ref> The song also peaked atop the ''Billboard'' [[Dance Club Songs|Dance Club Play]] chart and reached number eight on the ''Billboard'' [[Hot R&B Singles]] chart.<ref name="usrandb"/> "Together Again" was certified platinum by the [[RIAA]].<ref name="riaa"/> In Canada, it peaked at number two on the ''[[RPM (magazine)|RPM]]'' 100 Hit Tracks chart and reached number one on the ''RPM'' Dance chart.<ref name="canada"/><ref name="dancecan"/> In Australasia, "Together Again" also experienced success. In Australia, it debuted at number 18 on the issue dated December 7, 1997, peaking at number four and staying on the [[ARIA Singles Chart]] for 25 weeks and was certified platinum by the [[Australian Recording Industry Association]] (ARIA) for 70,000 copies shipped.<ref name=aus/><ref name="aria.com.au"/> In New Zealand, it debuted at number 16 the week of December 21, 1997. On February 22, 1998, it reached its peak of number five, staying on the chart for ten weeks.<ref name=nzl/>

The song debuted and peaked at number four on the [[UK Singles Chart]] on December 13, 1997, falling to six the following week, three weeks later it returned to its peak of four, spending ten weeks in the top ten and 19 weeks inside the chart.<ref name=ukpeak/> It was certified platinum by the [[British Phonographic Industry]] (BPI), selling 600,000 units in the UK.<ref name=ukcert/> It also spent a week atop the [[UK R&B Singles and Albums Charts|UK R&B Singles Chart]] and number six on the [[UK Dance Charts]].<ref name=ukrandb/><ref name=ukdance/> It is Jackson's best-selling UK single. It was certified platinum for 500,000 copies sold.<ref name=germany/><ref name=gercert/> In the Netherlands, "Together Again" entered the singles chart at number 61 during the week of December 13, 1997. It eventually peaked at number one, staying a total of thirty-two weeks on the chart.<ref name=net/> The Nederlandse Vereniging van Producenten en Importeurs van beeld- en geluidsdragers ([[NVPI]]) certified the single gold for shipment of 10,000 copies.<ref name="nvpi"/> On the Swiss Singles Chart dated January 11, 1998, "Together Again" debuted at number 13.<ref name=swi/> After two weeks, it peaked at number two and was later certified gold by the [[International Federation of the Phonographic Industry]] (IFPI).<ref name=swicert/> A portion of the single's worldwide sales were donated by Jackson to the [[American Foundation for AIDS Research]].<ref name="Jacksons Number Ones"/>

The song also peaked atop the Billboard Dance Club Play chart and reached number eight on the Billboard Hot R&B Singles chart. "Together Again" was certified platinum by the RIAA. In Canada, it peaked at number two on the RPM 100 Hit Tracks chart and reached number one on the RPM Dance chart. In Australasia, "Together Again" also experienced success. In Australia, it debuted at number 18 on the issue dated December 7, 1997, peaking at number four and staying on the ARIA Singles Chart for 25 weeks and was certified platinum by the Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) for 70,000 copies shipped. In New Zealand, it debuted at number 16 the week of December 21, 1997. On February 22, 1998, it reached its peak of number five, staying on the chart for ten weeks.

The song debuted and peaked at number four on the UK Singles Chart on December 13, 1997, falling to six the following week, three weeks later it returned to its peak of four, spending ten weeks in the top ten and 19 weeks inside the chart. It was certified platinum by the British Phonographic Industry (BPI), selling 600,000 units in the UK. It also spent a week atop the UK R&B Singles Chart and number six on the UK Dance Charts. It is Jackson's best-selling UK single. In Austria, it entered the singles chart at number 25, eventually peaking at number six and spending a total of fourteen weeks on the chart. In France, the song peaked at number two for ten weeks, and was certified platinum by the SNEP. In Germany, it peaked at number two for two weeks and remaining on the German Singles Chart for twenty-four weeks. It was certified platinum for 500,000 copies sold. In the Netherlands, "Together Again" entered the singles chart at number 61 during the week of December 13, 1997. It eventually peaked at number one, staying a total of thirty-two weeks on the chart. The Nederlandse Vereniging van Producenten en Importeurs van beeld- en geluidsdragers (NVPI) certified the single gold for shipment of 10,000 copies. On the Swiss Singles Chart dated January 11, 1998, "Together Again" debuted at number 13. After two weeks, it peaked at number two and was later certified gold by the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI). A portion of the single's worldwide sales were donated by Jackson to the American Foundation for AIDS Research.
